- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and prices drop, model underreacts; increase downward forecast momentum to match sentiment shift.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if forecast is trending upward from 80–85, cap max price at 85.5; if downward, floor at 78.5.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price drops after sentiment reversal; add 2–3% lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment to forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-day history to anchor forecast.
